haiku-low.q1: Sign-in still works. Only the unchanged Google sub is looked up, so they reach the same account. Google never changes users.email.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter the existing account's password on the confirm page. A correct password inserts the user_identities row, deletes the pending link, then calls start_session.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds one to failed_logins and reshows the page. The fifth locks the account for 15 minutes, deletes the pending link, and shows the locked message.
haiku-low.q4: Unmatched verified email: one transaction creates a passwordless user and its user_identities row, then start_session. Unverified: refused, nothing created, user told to use email and password.
haiku-low.q5: Both get an error page and nothing changes. At 12 minutes the Redis entry has expired. A repeat load finds the entry already deleted by the first callback.
haiku-low.q6: A normal sessions row via start_session. Any old sid session is deleted, a new sid cookie is set, and the user is redirected to next or /home.
haiku-low.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required; the session user must match the attempt's user. If the sub is linked to anyone, or the user already has Google, it is refused.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis under oauth:state:<state>, with a 10-minute TTL. The callback deletes it in one step; expiry also removes it. The browser's oauth cookie holds only state.
haiku-low.q9: Redis oauth:pending:<id> holds the user id and sub. The browser holds the id in an HttpOnly cookie. Success, lockout, or 10-minute expiry deletes it.
haiku-low.q10: In the new user_identities table. UNIQUE constraints on user_id and sub enforce one Google account per user and one user per Google account.
haiku-low.q11: An error page, and nothing changes. Whether the exchange is retried is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q12: Mode (login or link) is saved in the Redis attempt. Link attempts store the user id, and the callback refuses unless the current session user matches it.

sonnet.q1: They still reach the same account, because only `sub` is looked up (Google never changes users.email and we don't store Google's email). Known sub -> start_session for the linked user; lockout is not checked.
sonnet.q2: The user must be shown the confirm password page (pending link saved in Redis + cookie) and POST the correct password to /auth/google/confirm (existing lockout rules apply). Then the user_identities row is inserted, pending link deleted, failed_logins reset, and start_session is called.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins and shows the confirm page again; the fifth wrong one locks the account for 15 minutes, deletes the pending link and shows the locked message. The user must start over.
sonnet.q4: Verified email matching no user: in one DB transaction create a user (lowercased email, no password, email_verified_at now) and its user_identities row (rolls back both on failure), then start_session. If email_verified is false: refuse, point to email and password, nothing is created.
sonnet.q5: Error page and nothing changes. The state entry has a 10 minute TTL and is deleted on first read, so an expired, unknown or already-used state fails.
sonnet.q6: No new session type: the existing start_session creates a normal sessions row and sets the sid cookie. It first deletes any old sid session, then redirects to next (relative path only) or /home.
sonnet.q7: Neither: no password is asked and the emails need not match. The session user must be the user saved in the attempt. If the sub is already linked to anyone (or the user already has a Google account), it refuses, back on Settings, and nothing changes.
sonnet.q8: In Redis at oauth:state:<state> (state key, PKCE verifier, nonce, mode, next, user id for link), with a 10 minute TTL. The callback reads and deletes it in one step (once only); the oauth cookie holding state is also cleared.
sonnet.q9: In Redis at oauth:pending:<id> holding user id and sub; the browser holds the random id in an HttpOnly cookie. Deleted on success, on lockout, and by 10 minute TTL expiry.
sonnet.q10: In the new table user_identities (id, user_id, sub, created_at). The UNIQUE constraints on sub and on user_id (FK to users, ON DELETE CASCADE) enforce one Google account per user and one user per Google account.
sonnet.q11: An error page is shown and nothing changes. Retrying is NOT STATED (no retry is described; the attempt entry is already used up, so the user starts again).
sonnet.q12: By the mode saved in the attempt's Redis entry (login or link). For link, the user id is saved in the attempt, and the callback requires the current session's user to equal that saved user, otherwise error page.
